that is BELOW the requirement, and it is below it at the targeting step rather
than at the shredder. The 26S has 57x of headroom and the
per-substrate envelope reaches 11x, so neither of those is what stops a
20.3x pulse. What does not move is the SUBUNIT ABUNDANCE: the specificity
subunits change 1.5-fold over the cycle, and if b(t) were set by how
much receptor is present, the pulse could not be built. So EITHER the amplitude
comes from activating receptor that is already there -- phosphorylation,
pseudosubstrate release, localisation -- OR from modifying the SUBSTRATE so it
becomes visible to a receptor whose amount never changed. Loops 145 and 146
tested the second on annotation and both failed; the first has never been
tested here and cannot be, because abundance proteomics does not see it.
